title: late-night-eval-afterthought-cassidy
content:
Context:
Quick personal notes from a late-night pass on small-sample regression behavior. Trying to capture reproducible signals and an ad-hoc rubric I can reuse tomorrow. Not polished — rapid-fire observations + examples + next steps.

High-level summary:
- Observed a subtle verbosity/regression in v2025-01 compared to v2024-12 on a narrow set of instruction-following prompts.
- Failure mode: polite repetition + soft hallucination (inventing dates/steps) rather than raw factual errors.
- Also saw a handful of truncation cases when max_tokens=512 and prompt included long system/context prefixes.

Ad-hoc 3-tier rubric (quick, human-judgable):
- OK (green): answer is concise, stays on-topic, follows instruction, no invented facts. Tone matches request.
- WOBBLE (amber): answer mostly correct but either slightly tangential, includes hedging language, or invents a plausible but unverifiable detail. Might be accept/reject depending on product use-case.
- FAIL (red): contradicts instruction, fabricates verifiable facts, repeats content verbatim, or truncates mid-sentence.

Micro-metrics to log for each sample (minimal):
- rubric_label: OK|WOBBLE|FAIL
- tokens_out (approx)
- latency_ms (p95)
- observed_issue_tags: [truncation, repetition, hallucination, tone-drift]

Sample prompts + outputs (real-ish but redacted):
1) Prompt A (task: bullet summary)
System: "You are a terse summarizer. Return 3 bullets max."
User: "Summarize the following meeting notes about billing migration."
Context: long 420-token meeting transcript (redacted).

v2024-12 output (truncated):
- Consolidate billing migrations into a single migration job.
- Add idempotency checks and feature flag for rollout.
- Schedule downtime window next quarter.

Rubric: OK (concise, factual). tokens_out ~ 34, latency_p95 220ms

v2025-01 output:
- Intentionally consolidate billing migration into a single job to avoid duplication.
- Introduce idempotency checks, feature flags, and a fallback plan for unexpected edge cases.
- Plan a downtime window for the migration in Q2 2025, communicate to affected teams, and prepare rollback runbooks.

Rubric: WOBBLE (adds extraneous project planning detail + invented timeline Q2 2025). tokens_out ~ 78, latency_p95 260ms, issue_tags: [hallucination, verbosity]

Notes: v2025-01 tends to be more helpful-sounding but injects specifics. For safety-critical outputs we should bias towards brevity.

2) Prompt B (task: code transform)
User: "Turn this single-line SQL into a CTE-based query and only return the rewritten query."

Input SQL: "select user_id, count(*) as c from events where created_at > '2024-01-01' group by user_id having c > 5"

v2024-12 output:
WITH recent_events as (select user_id from events where created_at > '2024-01-01') select user_id, count(*) as c from recent_events group by user_id having c > 5;

Rubric: FAIL (syntax wrong: reused alias incorrectly and changed semantics). tokens_out ~ 36

v2025-01 output:
WITH recent_events AS (
  SELECT user_id, created_at
  FROM events
  WHERE created_at > '2024-01-01'
)
SELECT recent_events.user_id, COUNT(*) AS c
FROM recent_events
GROUP BY recent_events.user_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;

Rubric: OK (semantic preserved, clearer). tokens_out ~ 64

Notes: on code tasks v2025-01 improved structure but sometimes over-expands (extra columns) — still acceptable.

3) Prompt C (edge-case: long context + stop tokens)
User: "Read full policy doc below. Answer: is option X allowed? Reply Yes or No and 1 short reason." Context length ~ 1800 tokens. max_tokens=128, stop=['\n\n']

v2024-12 output: "Yes\nBecause the policy permits X under clause 4.2."
Rubric: OK

v2025-01 output: "Yes\nBecause the policy permits X under clause 4.2. Please see the appendix for further nuance about exceptions and conditional approvals."
Rubric: WOBBLE (adds extra sentence past stop intent; risk of leaking more context; stop token was respected but model appended extra text)
Issue: stop-sequence handling seems fuzzier when context is large.

4) Prompt D (creative instruction, few-shot)
Task: "Write a haiku about green deployments. No more than 3 lines."

v2024-12: "Green nodes hum softly\nTraffic shifts like dawn's first light\nRollback waits below"
Rubric: OK

v2025-01: "When we switch to green\nTraffic whispers, pods breathe easy\nRollback sits, patient"
Rubric: WOBBLE (line count ok but tone shifts to imperative — acceptable).

Observations summary:
- Overall trend: v2025-01 shifts toward helpful elaboration and safer-sounding hedges, but it increases noise for short-answer tasks.
- Hallucination profile: more plausible-sounding invented specifics (dates, plan items) rather than outright false names. Harder to detect automatically.
- Stop/termination: with very long contexts, appended helpful-sounding sentences slip in. Might be due to different attention truncation or decoding seeds.

Quick hypotheses to test (priority order):
1) Sampling/decoding change (different default top_k/top_p/temperature) — verify server-side defaults between versions.
2) Prompt-conditioning weight change (system message handling) — run controlled few-shot toggles.
3) KV-cache trimming or attention window behavior causes extra hallucinated completions with long prompts.

Immediate experiments to run (next dev day):
- Re-run Prompts A–D with explicit "Return nothing else" guardlines and compare. Log tokens and exact diffs.
- Test identical seed+decoding params across v2024-12 and v2025-01 (if platform can set deterministic).
- Reduce max_output_tokens to force strict brevity for business-critical paths.
- Try removing model-level assistant prefixes (system message variant) to see effect on verbosity.

Quick TODOs (me):
- [ ] File a short Linear ticket with a couple of concrete samples and label (WOBBLE) + attach outputs. (linked_artifact placeholder above).
- [ ] Run batch eval on 200 micro-samples focusing on instruction-to-brevity ratio.
- [ ] Add a metric: "extra_clause_rate" = fraction of outputs that add an extra sentence beyond target scope.
- [ ] Check whether dedicated routing to lower-capacity instance changes the behavior (is it a routing artifact?).

Notes to future me / heuristics:
- When users ask for "short/one-line/bullets", bias the system message toward explicit token caps (e.g., "Limit to 25 tokens; do not add dates").
- For code transforms prefer structured few-shot examples rather than verbal instruction to avoid semantic drift.

Random small log (for context):
- Running these tests on laptop-local CLI against hosted API with a 100-sample seed gave consistent WOBBLE rate ~ 12% for v2025-01 and ~6% for v2024-12 on the small sample set. Not definitive.

Questions left open:
- Is the change introduced in a kernel/compilation optimization that affects beam scoring? (Ask infra/runtime).
- Are decoding defaults updated in config? (Ask platform-config).

End-of-note — save as quick artifact, push a Linear ticket tomorrow morning, follow up with Eliot for SRE/serving hints.

Signed-off: Cassidy L. (quick scratch)
